newsitem.title: UK: Sterling surges as Brown dampens ERM speculation.
newsitem.headline: Sterling surges as Brown dampens ERM speculation.

text.p: The British pound accelerated almost two pfennigs higher in afternoon trade in London after finance minister Gordon Brown said the UK was not proposing to re-enter Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).

The comments lifted the pound, which had bounced from a seven-week low of 2.7245 marks earlier in the day, because they threw cold water on a report last week that the UK may re-enter the ERM at a central target rate of 2.50 marks -- more than twenty pfennigs below current levels.
"We have no plans to re-join the ERM," Brown said.
Traders said conditions were nervous and volatile.

"The comments from Brown seemed to rule out a return to the ERM and were the trigger for the rally. A modest recovery in the dollar late the day also seemed to help," said Jeremy Stretch, foreign exchange strategist at NatWest Markets.

"The market is very volatile at the moment, however, and a lot of people were caught by surprise," said Stretch. "I think we can expect more of the same sort of volatility until the issue is cleared up a bit better."
At 1550 GMT, the pound was trading at 2.7672/82 marks, up more than 3-1/2 pfennigs from the close in Europe on Friday and up from about 2.7450 marks just before Brown spoke.
Against the dollar, it was at $1.6234/39 compared with $1.6208/18 late last week.

"The decline in sterling/mark last week on the (ERM) rumour was overdone, and it's now clear that the new government doesn't mean to take Britain back into the ERM," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International. "There's been no change (in Britain's stance). The UK's options are being kept wide open."

Brown also said he did not think the Maastricht Treaty criterion insisting on ERM membership for two years before starting European monetary union was cast in stone. This was the stance of the previous UK government and is backed by Sweden.
Yet, traders said the fact Brown was keen to keep his EMU options open would limit any recovery of the pound.

"A more pro-European Labour government will keep talk of eventual EMU participation bubbling in the background and any fixing rate for EMU will not be up at 4-1/2 year highs, regardless of ERM," said a trader at a U.S. bank here.
The pound surged to 2.8330 marks last week -- its highest level since it was forced to leave the ERM in September 1992.
The additional fillip came after the new UK Labour government, in power since May 2, announced an expected quarter- point rise in UK base rates to 6.25 percent last Tuesday.

The rate rise was bolstered by an announcement that in future the Bank of England would have operational independence in setting UK interest rates -- a move towards the central bank independence required by Maastricht before joining EMU.
A retreat of the dollar across the board and last week's story about the 2.50-mark ERM re-entry level precipitated sterling's subsequent retreat.
